candidate.answerReason: Changing to base 10 gives numerator log10(12)=2a+b and nonzero denominator log10(5)=1-a.

methods.label: Change to the given logarithm base
methods.explanation:
The given logarithms have base \(10\), so changing to that base lets us use \(a\) and \(b\) directly:
\[
\log_5 12=\frac{\log_{10}12}{\log_{10}5}.
\]
Since \(12=2^2\cdot3\), the product and power rules give
\[
\log_{10}12=2a+b.
\]
Also, \(5=10/2\), so
\[
\log_{10}5=1-a.
\]
This denominator is positive because \(5>1\). Therefore
\[
\log_5 12=\frac{2a+b}{1-a},
\]
which is choice D.
